agenda.2026-11-23-israel-banque-centrale: Israel: the central bank sets its rate

The Bank of Israel announces its decision on 23 November, with its rate currently at 3.25% [1]. Inflation fell to 1.1% year on year in October, making a quarter-point cut to 3% more likely [2]: borrowing would become slightly cheaper.
agenda.2026-11-23-nigeria-banque-central: Nigeria: the central bank sets its rate

The Central Bank of Nigeria's monetary policy committee meets on 23 and 24 November [1], two months after cutting its rate from 26.5% to 23% [2]. Inflation eased again to 14.06% in October [3], leaving room for another cut.
agenda.2026-11-25-etats-unis-pib-pce.tit: United States: Q3 GDP and October PCE inflation
agenda.2026-11-25-etats-unis-pib-pce.why: On the same day, the Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes its second estimate of July-September growth and October household income and spending, including the PCE price index watched by the Fed [1][2]. These figures land two weeks before the Fed's 8 December meeting.
agenda.2026-11-28-taiwan-elections-local: About 19.65 million voters choose mayors, county chiefs, councillors and village heads, more than 11,000 posts in all [1][2]. It is a national test for the ruling party (DPP) against the Kuomintang and the TPP, which are discussing an alliance [1]: a DPP setback would weigh on Taipei's line towards Beijing.
agenda.2026-11-28-australie-victoria-ele: Voters in Victoria, Australia's second most populous state, elect a new parliament on 28 November; voting is compulsory [1][2]. The result will decide who governs the state and leads its choices on housing, local taxes and major projects.
agenda.2026-12-09-kenya-banque-centrale-: Kenya: the central bank sets its rate

The Central Bank of Kenya's monetary policy committee meets on 9 December [1], after holding its rate at 8.75% on 7 October [2]. Its decision affects the cost of credit for Kenyan households and businesses.
agenda.2026-12-15-hongrie-banque-central: Hungary: the central bank's last rate decision of the year

The Monetary Council of the Hungarian National Bank holds its last rate meeting of the year on 15 December [1]. It cut its rate by 0.25 points to 5.50% in August [2]: another cut would make credit cheaper but could weaken the forint.
agenda.2026-12-17-philippines-banque-cen: Philippines: the central bank's last rate decision of the year

The Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas holds its last regular meeting of the year on 17 December [1][2]. It raised rates in June [3]: its decision matters for the peso and the cost of credit in the Philippines.
